## Summary

Research confidence is **Low**. Sources do not yet confirm this break's best wind. It is the class the app computes from the evidence (how well the break's ideal conditions are documented), not a forecast and not a probability.

Main gaps:

- Sources disagree about the best wind direction.
- No survey, scientific or official source confirms the wave size this break works in.
- No survey, scientific or official source describes the shape of the bottom.
- No survey, scientific or official source describes how the wave breaks.

| Variable | Research confidence | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| Swell direction | High | Supported by 4 independent sources, including a forecast site's spot guide. |
| Swell size | Moderate | Supported by 3 independent sources, including a surf magazine. |
| Swell period | Moderate | Supported by 2 independent sources, including a forecast site's spot guide. |
| Wind | Low | Supported by 3 independent sources, including a surf magazine; 2 disagree. |
| Tide | High | Supported by 3 independent sources, including a forecast site's spot guide; 1 disagrees. |
| Bottom / bathymetry | Moderate | Described by 4 independent sources, including an encyclopedia entry. |
| Season | High | Supported by 4 independent sources, including an encyclopedia entry. |
| How the wave breaks | Moderate | Described by 3 independent sources, including an encyclopedia entry. |

Research notes (research_evidence.json):

> Eleven sources from eight publishers; nine were read directly. The two Surfer Today pages returned 403 (Cloudflare) and are kept unchanged as web_search. No peer-reviewed, official or survey source was found; Crossref returned nothing for Dungeons or Hout Bay. Wind: N-centred winds agree with the profile's 30. WannaSurf (both entries) gives N/NW/NE, Yeeew N, and Surfer Today N or NW-NE. Surf-Forecast's NW (315) contradicts. surfing.world, an unattributed and possibly machine-written blog, says a light SE wind is best; this is a weak outlier. Stormrider's Dungeons page holds 'Northerly' wind, 'Low to Mid tide', S-W swell and 10-30+ ft. Those values are only in the page's script data and were not recorded. Tide: low or low-to-mid from Surf-Forecast, Yeeew and Surfer Today agrees. WannaSurf's main entry says all tides. The Slab section prefers mid to high and gets super shallow at lower tides; that is section-specific and not compared. Size: WannaSurf's minimum is 12 ft (Slab 6 ft), Yeeew's is triple overhead (about 18 ft), and Surfing-Waves says it only works on big swells. Both record waves (47 ft swell and the 65 ft Greg Long ride) were dropped. Period: only Surfer Today (unreadable) gives 15-19 s. A Ticket to Ride camp blog says Cape Town rarely gets periods over 15 s, which suggests the profile's 17 s ideal is uncommon. Bathymetry: the reef depths (2.5 m and 3.5 m) come from Wikipedia, not a hydrographic survey. Stormrider's Cape Peninsula region page only names Dungeons as a big-wave venue and was not recorded. Unreachable: surfsisters.co.za (no response) and brandsouthafrica.com (404). Seasonality: winter, from Jun-Aug up to Apr-Sep; it agrees.

## Ideal conditions

Directions are compass degrees the swell or wind comes FROM, ranges clockwise. Heights keep the scale each source states (breaking face, Hawaiian, swell or relative to the surfer); the app's sizes are breaking face heights in feet. Sources are numbered as in [Sources](#sources).

### Swell height

| Field | Research value | Status | Sources | App model setting |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Minimum suitable | 12 ft | documented | S4, S8 | `wave_height_min_ft` 15 ft (breaking face) |
| Ideal range | triple overhead to tow-in size | documented | S7 | no separate setting; working range 15–50 ft |
| Maximum suitable | 16 ft | documented | S4, S8 | `wave_height_max_ft` 50 ft (breaking face) |

Notes:

- **Minimum suitable**: WannaSurf says it starts working at over 3.5 m / 12 ft (the page's own conversion; face or offshore height not stated), and Surfing-Waves says it only starts working on the big swells, without a number.
  - S4 (WannaSurf): “Swell sizeStarts working at Over 3.5m / 12ft and holds up to 5m / 16 ft and over”
  - S8 (Surfing-Waves.com): “Can hold huge waves and only starts working on the big swells.”
- **Ideal range**: Yeeew says it gets good between triple overhead and tow-in size, a face height relative to the surfer with no number in feet.
  - S7 (Yeeew!): “It gets good between triple overhead and tow-in size.”
- **Maximum suitable**: WannaSurf's top bracket is 5 m / 16 ft and over (open-ended, scale not stated) and Surfing-Waves says it can hold huge waves; no excerpt gives an upper limit.
  - S4 (WannaSurf): “Swell sizeStarts working at Over 3.5m / 12ft and holds up to 5m / 16 ft and over”
  - S8 (Surfing-Waves.com): “Can hold huge waves and only starts working on the big swells.”

Notes:

- **Ideal**: Surfer Today (search summary) reports one guide giving the ideal swell as a long-period (15-19 s) groundswell from the west; it is the only number.
  - S6 (Surfer Today): “One guide says its ideal swell is a long-period (15-19 seconds) groundswell from the west.”
- **Acceptable**: No excerpt states an acceptable range of swell periods.
- **Short-period behaviour**: No excerpt describes how the break handles short-period swell or windswell.
- **Long-period behaviour**: Ticket to Ride says Cape Town very rarely sees periods over about 15 seconds and that the swell period makes the wave cleaner and more defined.
  - S9 (Ticket to Ride (surf camp)): “In Cape Town we very rarely see swell periods materialise over about 15 seconds...What the swell period does is makes the wave cleaner and more defined from one to the next.”

  - S1 (Surf-Forecast.com): “Dungeons in Cape Peninsula is a sheltered reef break that only works once in a while.”
  - S8 (Surfing-Waves.com): “Can hold huge waves and only starts working on the big swells.”

  - S6 (Surfer Today): “One guide says its ideal swell is a long-period (15-19 seconds) groundswell from the west.”

## Conflicting information

- **Wind · offshore**: Yeeew (north), WannaSurf (N, NW, NE) and Surfer Today (search summaries: NW-NE, a light northerly) centre on north, Surf-Forecast says offshore is northwest (315 deg, 45 deg from north), and an unattributed surfing.world blog says a light southeast wind is best.
- **Tide · preferred stage**: Surf-Forecast and Surfer Today (search summary) say low tide, Surfer Today's other guide and Yeeew say low to mid, while WannaSurf says all tides.
- **Seasonality · prime months**: All sources say the austral winter but disagree on its length: Wikipedia and surfing.world give June to August (Surf-Forecast says winter), while Surfer Today (search summaries) reports one guide giving May to August and another April to September.
